original_value: Building dialogue systems that can converse naturally with humans is a challenging yet intriguing problem of artificial intelligence. In open-domain human-computer conversation, where the conversational agent is expected to respond to human utterances in an interesting and engaging way, commonsense knowledge has to be integrated into the model effectively. In this paper, we investigate the impact of providing commonsense knowledge about the concepts covered in the dialogue. Our model represents the first attempt to integrating a large commonsense knowledge base into end-to-end conversational models. In the retrieval-based scenario, we propose a model to jointly take into account message content and related commonsense for selecting an appropriate response. Our experiments suggest that the knowledge-augmented models are superior to their knowledge-free counterparts.

result.paraphrase: Creating dialogue systems that can converse naturally with people is a challenging but fascinating AI problem. In open-domain human-computer conversation, where the conversational agent is expected to reply to human utterances in an interesting and engaging manner, commonsense knowledge must be incorporated into the model effectively. This paper examines the effect of supplying commonsense knowledge about the concepts used in the dialogue. Our model is the first effort to integrate a large commonsense knowledge base into end-to-end conversational models. For retrieval-based settings, we introduce a model that jointly considers message content and related commonsense knowledge when choosing an appropriate response. Our experiments indicate that knowledge-augmented models outperform their knowledge-free counterparts.
